info.album: Oh Happy Day: The Best Of The Edwin Hawkins Singers

podcast.body: The Edwin Hawkins Singers took this traditional hymn and transformed it into a pop hit in 1968, making it one of the first, if not the first, gospel songs to achieve such mainstream success. This move drew criticism from churches who disapproved of their singers profiting from hymns. Despite the backlash, Edwin Hawkins believed young people needed songs like "Oh Happy Day" as they were turning away from the church but remained confused about life, seeing music as a way to "take the gospel to them." The song's success inspired George Harrison to write "My Sweet Lord." "In 1968, Edwin Hawkins took this hymn and crafted it into a pop hit."
